title: The guard's shell-write scan runs in linear time, so a long command is judged, not timed out
why: hooks/guard.py _shell_could_write (~621-630) is quadratic in a command's word count: it calls _shell_write_hit with an accept-all predicate, which defeats the cheap-predicate-first order. It runs on every cloud own-session Bash call. Measured on commands with no write word: 300 words 0.29 s, 1000 words 2.3 s, 2000 words 9 s, 6000 words 77 s. Past about 5000 words the hook times out and the call runs unjudged. No test pins it.
note: Lane revive-1042 (#1971 round 3 at a7a3a67ac, 13:55 CST Nov 9), filed as a debt candidate; a step because every Bash call pays it and a long heredoc reaches 1000 words. Fix: a one-regex pre-scan, or writes-first order, plus a cloud scaling case. Related: step frozen-crash-followups (another quadratic judge), export-page-cookie-linear.
